findings.F1: The book fails on its falls, not its gain. Its deepest fall is −23.7 % and lasts 903 days, against a yearly return of +12.3 %, so Calmar is 0.51. Inside that fall, the Sunday cases in the three lowest quintiles of s20/s60 lost −0.60, −0.55 and −1.18 (summed bar gains after costs), while the top two quintiles earned +0.32 and +0.78.
findings.F2: The reversal sits in the high-volatility-ratio cases. By quintile of s20/s60, the signed 2-day return is +0.76 % (t 2.6), +0.13 % (t 0.4), −0.18 % (t −0.5), +0.80 % (t 2.4) and +2.10 % (t 5.0), over about 520 cases each. The book's gain per case after costs is negative in the first three quintiles (−0.01 %, −0.06 %, −0.14 %) and +0.43 % and +1.25 % in the top two.
findings.F3: A rebuilt book that trades the Sunday bets only when s20/s60 is at or above its 60th percentile raises Calmar from 0.51 to 0.84. It does this by cutting the deepest fall from −23.7 % to −10.0 %, with Sharpe 0.90 against 0.74 and a yearly return of +8.3 %. At the 80th percentile, Calmar is 0.93 (fall −7.1 %, Sharpe 0.99, yearly return +6.7 %).
findings.F4: The volatility condition is not an effect of its own. On non-Sunday bars, betting against the 1-day move over the next 2 days earns −0.25 % (t −1.5, n 1490) in the lowest s20/s60 quintile and +0.20 % (t 1.0, n 1646) in the top one. Sunday cases in the top quintile earn +2.10 % (t 5.0). The weekend situation carries the effect, and the condition fits the theory: thin weekend books push price furthest when volatility has just risen.
findings.F5: The book's gain is concentrated in its strongest forecasts. The top quintile of |forecast| has a mean signed return of +1.36 % (t 4.9) and carries a summed gain of 10.0 out of about 14.8. The lowest quintile earns −0.12 at a mean allocation of 0.02.
findings.F6: Both sides lose in the deepest fall: short bets after weekend rises −0.88 and long bets after weekend falls −1.44. Both sides are positive over all cases (+0.79 %, t 5.1 and +0.56 %, t 3.8). Leaving out one side does not repair the falls.
findings.F7: The reversal is spread over both days, with 49 % of the signed 2-day move on Monday.

ideas.idea: A coin's Saturday-to-Sunday close-to-close return reverses over the next 2 days (Monday and Tuesday), only while its 20-day daily volatility is above its 60-day daily volatility. Within that state, the move back is larger the further 20-day volatility exceeds 60-day volatility.
ideas.consequence: A trader would take the Sunday-close bet against the weekend move only when recent volatility has risen above its longer norm, and stay out otherwise, where the reversal is too small to pay for its falls.
ideas.name: weekend reversal in rising volatility

ideas.idea: A coin's Saturday-to-Sunday close-to-close return reverses over the next 2 days (Monday and Tuesday). The move back grows steeply, more than in proportion, with how far the coin's 20-day daily volatility sits above its 60-day daily volatility, so the largest reversals come in the cases where recent volatility is furthest above its norm.
ideas.consequence: A trader would concentrate the Sunday-close reversal bet in the coins whose recent volatility has jumped furthest above their longer norm, rather than spreading it across all weekend moves.
ideas.name: steep volatility-graded weekend reversal
